subject: Compiler warning when using manual example

messages.author: 6b3b475e6af83898
messages.subject: Compiler warning when using manual example
parts:
I'm working on an IRT with the effects of various student demographic predictors varying by country, so am adapting the example on p. 95 of the manual.

In the compile phase, it comes back with:

> Warning (non-fatal): sampling statement (~) contains a transformed parameter or local variable.
> You must increment lp__ with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.

This is because the example code (and my modified version thereof) opens the model with:

> matrix[K,K] Sigma_beta;
> Sigma_beta <- diag_matrix(tau) * Omega * diag_matrix(tau);

The prospect of incrementing lp__ by hand (or through increment_log_prob) scares me a bit, so I'd like guidance on the right way to proceed without breaking anything. And the manual should be updated to incorporate those same fixes.

Thanks,
Josh

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compiler warning when using manual example
parts:
That's a false positive from the parser, and I'm not
seeing it in v2.2.0's parser, at least through RStan.

But I just updated the conditions for this warning extensively
for the next release to remove false positives from linear transforms.
You only need a Jacobian adjustment for a non-linear transform, and
we were spitting out far too many false-positive warnings.

The error would've been from another statement, anway, because it's
only triggered on sampling statements.

The comment on Omega needs to be changed because it's the prior
correlation, not covariance. And note on the next page of the manual
that it's more efficient to use diag_pre_multiply() and diag_post_multiply().
I noted the comment udate at:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/567

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compiler warning when using manual example
parts:
Thanks. I’m building up to those optimizations, to be sure I understand what each step does and see how it changes the performance.

And yeah, I should have said that the error is triggered later by:

> for (j in 1:J)
> beta[j] ~ multi_normal((u[j] * gamma)’, Sigma_beta);

(although since I don’t have group predictors, I just have: beta[j] ~ multi_normal(mu_A,Sigma_alpha), with mu_A in the parameter block.)

I’m using rstan 2.2.0, also.
